subject: OpenWater discovery: infra, SLOs, and deployment recommendation

Subject: OpenWater discovery: infra, SLOs, and deployment recommendation

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we captured the right priorities and to outline the next steps. If anything below is off, tell me and I’ll update.

High-level pain & goals (what you said):
- Production latency sensitivity: p95 target <= 120ms for short prompts (~256 tokens).
- Peak concurrency: ~1,200 concurrent requests during batch windows; sustained baseline ~150 qps.
- Cost sensitivity: target run-rate under $0.18 / 1k tokens for generation workloads.
- Regulatory: customer data must remain in your VPC for EU customers; US workloads can use Redwood Hosted.

Technical items we discussed:
- Model: you indicated interest in an LLaMA-3 family (33B) fine-tuned for retrieval-augmented generation.
- KV caching: expected high prefix reuse on support workflows; looking for cache hit >= 60%.
- SLOs: 99.9% availability for inference; automated fallback to cheaper, smaller model during bursts.
- Deployment preference: Dedicated reserved pool for US public traffic + Private (VPC) for EU regulated workloads.

Immediate next steps (proposal):
1) I’ll put together a topology recommendation (dedicated pool sizing, AZ distribution, GPU type options) and an SLO/cost matrix — deliver by EOD Wednesday.
2) Rishi will do a quick cost/throughput simulation and recommended quantization profile for the 33B variant.
3) Can you loop in Procurement (procure@openwater.ai) so we can start discussing terms and any required compliance paperwork?

Attachments: I’ll include an initial SLO matrix and topology sketch in the next email.

Thanks — great conversation.

— Soojin

Soojin —

Thanks, this looks right. Couple of clarifications / numbers from our side that will affect sizing:
- Typical prompt length: 40–320 tokens (mode ~120).
- Average generated tokens per request: ~90 tokens.
- Concurrency distribution: spikes to ~1,200 concurrent for 30–90s after marketing pushes; average sustained qps 120–180.
- P95 goal: 120ms for simple chat completions; we can accept 300–400ms for longer (>1k token) multi-turn sessions.
- Budget: we’re targeting ~$25k–35k/mo initially for inference spend while we validate.

On compliance: we’ll need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a brief on data residency controls for EU traffic. Looping Procurement and the CTO.

I’ve OKed receiving the SLO/cost matrix and the topology sketch. Also, happy to share a sample prompt set if Rishi wants to run a quick bench.

Subject: RE: OpenWater discovery: infra, SLOs, and deployment recommendation

Alex / Soojin —

I took the numbers Alex shared and sketched an initial technical recommendation. Summary below; attaching the detailed SLO matrix and cost scenarios (openwater_slo_matrix.xlsx).

Summary recommendations (short):
- Topology: Dedicated reserved cluster (US) using H100s for the 33B fine-tuned model; Private VPC deployment for EU customers pinned to customer-managed subnet. Multi-AZ replication for leader-follower evens out availability.
- Model execution: quantize to 8-bit (Q8) with KV cache enabled. Expect ~2.2x throughput improvement vs fp16 with small quality delta for your use-case.
- Autoscaling: target steady pool for baseline 150 qps with headroom to 1,500 concurrent tokens using fast scale-up (burst nodes) and graceful model-fallback policy: 33B -> 13B if queueing > 200ms for >60s.
- Latency expectation: with batching set to 16 requests and sequence length ~256 tokens, p95 target of 120ms is achievable on H100 with proper KV warmup; A100 likely hits ~180–220ms.
- Cache: with expected 60% prefix reuse, we project token-cost reduction of ~18% and effective p95 improvements for repeated flows.

Operational notes:
- Warm start and KV prefill is critical for marketing spikes — recommend pre-warming jobs triggered by your event plan.
- Canary rollout: Redwood supports traffic-splitting and automatic rollback on quality regressions (monitor by prompt set).

Cost ballpark (monthly) given your volumes and Q8 quantization:
- H100 dedicated pool + networking & storage: estimated $28k–$38k / month (depends on commit level and burst policy).
- Lower-cost A100 option: $20k–$28k / month but increased p95 risk.

Next technical deliverables I’ll produce by Thursday EOD:
- Detailed topology PDF (recommended_topology.pdf).
- SLO x cost workbook (openwater_slo_matrix.xlsx).

If Alex can drop the sample prompts, I’ll run a short benchmark (throughput and p95 by model/quant).

— Rishi
